pictures.author: Nuno Sequeira Andre
pictures.observations: Entire960x720 ordinary wide chapel interior inspected. Three aisles, bone-covered round piers, transverse/diagonal groin-vault ribs and pale painted ceiling panels, skull/bone wall fields, narrow high side windows, dark floor panels with pale joint bands and gilded framed altar. Eight pier stations/five bays and hidden details remain a picture-led allocation.

pictures.author: Ken & Nyetta
pictures.observations: Entire960x638 ordinary altar/pier detail inspected. Gilded paired twisted columns, layered cornice/pediment and cross inside a framed central panel, panelled altar table, bone-covered cylindrical shafts with pale base/capital bands and original scroll/rosette vocabulary on vaults. Museum barriers differ between dates and are omitted; no copied paintings, inscription or sacred narrative atlas.

pictures.author: PESP/Wikimedia
pictures.observations: Entire960x720 ordinary host exterior inspected. Tall ashlar nave, sloping west front with pointed/traceried central window, low pointed-arch portico with buttress piers, crenellated parapets and corner conical pinnacles/cross. Connected white lower ranges with pale stone window surrounds, dark openings and tiled roofs. Earlier Evora02 crop was insufficient for the whole silhouette and is not retained.

pictures.author: Nuno Sequeira Andre
pictures.observations: Entire960x720 ordinary chapel entry inspected. Actual open rectangular stone portal, paired smooth shafts/leaf-like capitals, heavy horizontal inscription lintel and raised pediment/corner finials, white vestibule and blue/pale lower tile vocabulary. Original plain lintel/scroll geometry used; no readable copied inscription, painting or narrative tile atlas.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Specific Capela dos Ossos interior and connected São Francisco exterior envelope: traversable entry vestibule/stone portal, three-aisle hall with eight bone-covered piers, pale groin vaults/ribs and original simplified ceiling scrolls, dense original skull/long-bone wall vocabulary, high side openings, dark/pale banded floor and simplified gilded twisted-column altar/cross. Host includes mapped stone nave/pointed west portico, crenellated gable/parapets and conical corner pinnacles, connected white lower ranges/shared tiled roofs. Chapel is an interior allocation inside the named host, not a separate building shell. No copied religious painting, readable inscription or photographic bone atlas; no full host church/museum interior.
